findings.problem: Design 4.1 asks that the CoM path before the command frame be array_equal between the stop and the turn. As generate actually runs them it is not: the preview grid step is the smallest frame interval of the whole commanded plan, so the turn's shorter strides after the command change the grid, the gains and with them the CoM before the command. The test was weakened to pass: exact equality only when both are forced onto the turn's grid, 0.05 mm on their own grids. The size is far below every gate, but 'nothing before the command knows' holds to micrometres, not bit for bit, and the rule text and design say otherwise.
findings.fix: Lead's choice, before any causal reference is frozen. Either (a) keep the code and say so: amend RULES['S2A-causal'] and design 4.1 to 'equal up to the preview grid step (under 0.05 mm of CoM)', keeping the test as it is; or (b) make it exact: give com_path_causal a grid step that does not depend on the commanded plan (for instance the walk's frame interval times the smallest factor of STRIDE_GRID, a.period * 0.60 / 160, for every causal move), then assert array_equal on the moves' own grids in the test and drop the dt= argument from it. (b) changes every causal reference's numbers and needs the stop and turn rebuilt.
findings.evidence: On 75-M-H-10 with Stage 1's nominal walk, the same two moves as the test: grid step 7.098 ms (stop) and 5.678 ms (turn); own grids, frames up to and including the command: array_equal False, largest difference 7.49e-06 m, at the command frame 4.9e-06 and 6.7e-06 m (x, y); against the walk's own LIPM path 8.3e-06 m (stop) and 1.07e-05 m (turn). The mutant that previews the commanded plan from the first step (k_switch = 0) and the one that switches one grid step early are both killed by this test, so the test does guard the preview information itself.

verdict: The legacy claim holds for everything I checked, and nothing in this review found bit-identity lost. Through my own script (not the builder's CLI) and the CLI itself I regenerated 11 distinct Stage 1 transitions at the full 6 passes, 6 on 75-M-H-10 and 5 on 60-N-T-10, covering a start, stops, in-place starts and stops, turn entries and exits and speed changes; all ten script outputs are byte-identical (cmp) to the restored Stage 1 files, their sha256 equal stage1/runs/2026-11-08/<body>/transitions.json and the entries of stage2/sets/legacy_check.json, and writing by path or through a file object gives the same hash. The other 25 I did not regenerate: for those I checked only that the record's 36 hashes equal Stage 1's json and the restored files, and that its moves.py hash, panel-source hash and versions are those of the wt/wp-m tree. The fast tests pass (23 passed, 2 skipped), also followed by Stage 1's transition tests in one session (29 passed), and with no restored inputs they skip cleanly (18 passed, 7 skipped, nothing written, no stage1/models). Importing moves changes neither the gait accuracy nor the thread variables; the CLI refuses an inherited OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and sets the three variables before numpy loads; only the three owned files differ from the working branch; the record is tracked and not ignored; both slow tests are behind STAGE2_SLOW. Each of the 20 fast test functions was killed by at least one of 34 mutants. Two things should be settled before merge or freeze: the slow test test_stop_and_turn_from_v0 is red at HEAD because the V0 quick right turn misses the consistency gate (2.758 mm against 2.5 mm, pass_ false; the stop passes), which is a ruling for the lead and not a constant to change; and the record's currency test does not look at the panels' sources, against which the record is already stale on the working branch (6a316fc8 against 4583a187), so the legacy check must be rerun on the merged tree and the test tightened. The remaining findings are minor: untested gate comparisons and unpinned gate constants, the accuracy left at r2 by kinematic and legacy_check, a pre-command CoM that depends on the commanded plan at the 7 micrometre level against the design's array_equal, a log file written by the default suite, and per-body provenance lost in the record. Not run by me: the slow legacy test (the builder's log shows its five names equal) and tests/test_stage2_look.py.
